title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the opening page of a section titled 'Moduli of elliptic curves: transcendental theory'. Grothendieck sets up the classical analytic description of complex elliptic curves in a coordinate-free way, as a prelude to describing the moduli as a period domain.

(1)–(4) A complex elliptic curve E is equivalent to two pieces of data. The first is the 1-dimensional complex vector space V = t_E, the tangent space at the origin. The second is a lattice Π ⊂ V, a discrete free Z-submodule of rank 2. In modern terms Π = H_1(E,Z), embedded in V by the exponential (uniformization) map. From Π alone one recovers:
- the real 2-dimensional vector space V ≅ Π⊗_Z R = Π_R;
- the real Lie group E ≅ V/Π ≅ Π_R/Π.
The complex structure on E is exactly a complex vector-space structure on V, which passes to the quotient. So the moduli problem becomes: the fixed topological datum (Π, Π_R), together with a variable complex structure on Π_R.

(5)–(7) For a real 2-dimensional V, a complex structure (an R-automorphism u with u² = −id) is equivalent to a complex line L ⊂ V_C = V⊗_R C such that the projection Re: V_C → V, z ↦ ½(z+z̄), restricts to an R-isomorphism φ: L ≅ V. This condition holds precisely when L is not the complexification of a real line, i.e. L ∩ L̄ = 0. Such L form P(V_C) \ P(V_R), the union of the upper and lower half-planes (one component per orientation).

The next page fixes the convention. The structure on V is the conjugate of the one transported from L, ux = −φ(iφ^{-1}x). Conversely, given u, one takes L = Ker(ψ: V_C → V_c) = {x + iux}, the −i-eigenspace of u_C (the (0,1)-part). Re: L → V is then antilinear. A margin note says this convention is chosen so that holomorphic and antiholomorphic forms come out correctly, i.e. so that it fits Hodge theory.

This is the standard first step toward realizing the moduli of complex elliptic curves as SL_2(Z)\H, via Hodge structures of weight ±1 on Π.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. The equivalence in (5)–(7) needs dim_R V = 2 and L a complex line; this is stated in an insertion ('de rang 2').
The orientation/sign convention is left implicit here and only fixed (as the conjugate structure) on the next page. Read alone, the page does not say which half-plane corresponds to which structure.

ideas.what: A complex elliptic curve is equivalent to a 1-dimensional C-vector space t_E with a rank-2 lattice; E ≅ t_E/Π ≅ Π_R/Π as a real Lie group.
ideas.modern_name: Analytic uniformization of complex tori / elliptic curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weierstrass, Jacobi, Abel (19th century); standard textbook material

ideas.what: Complex structures on a real 2-plane V correspond to complex lines L ⊂ V⊗C with L ∩ L̄ = 0 (Re|_L an isomorphism). L is taken as the (0,1)/−i-eigenspace, giving P^1(C) \ P^1(R).
ideas.modern_name: Hodge structures of weight 1 / Hodge filtration; period domain (upper and lower half-planes)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; formalized by Griffiths (period domains) and Deligne (Hodge theory II, 'Travaux de Griffiths')

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an elementary, carefully coordinate-free exposition of standard material: the analytic uniformization of elliptic curves, and complex structures as complex lines in the complexification. Its only notable feature is the deliberate choice of the conjugate/antiholomorphic convention to match Hodge theory, which is routine.
